analysis.title: Skipper Warsh and his Hawkish Crew: FOMC Preview October 2026
key_insights: Rabobank expects the FOMC to hold the target range at 3.75-4.00% at the October 27-28 meeting.
Rabobank expects Hammack, Kashkari and Logan to repeat their July dissents in favor of a hike, so the hold is not unanimous.

Chair Warsh is expected to keep refusing forward guidance at the press conference but to do so in a hawkish way, as at Jackson Hole. He may say underlying inflation trends have not meaningfully improved without saying a hike is coming soon.
Rabobank expects the next hike, 25 bps, at the December 8-9 meeting. It sees strong committee support, and rising CPI inflation from higher oil prices should raise the probability of that hike.
The FOMC unanimously raised the range by 25 bps to 3.75-4.00% in September. The September projections showed a hawkish shift in the Fed's reaction function.

Skipping October lets the Committee see more data, and a December hike would bring the funds rate to the median participant's year-end projection. Skipping also avoids a hike less than a week before the midterm elections. President Trump has said he wants lower rates.

Four participants' dots in the September plot showed two more 25 bps hikes by year-end. Holding in October makes that path impossible, so those four do not want to hold. Rabobank thinks three of them are the July dissenters, who are voters.
Rabobank's baseline is that the Fed stays on hold through 2027, in line with the September median dot, but the risk is to the upside because it expects inflation to rise further in coming months.

Futures price about three hikes from now, while the September median dot shows one more hike in 2026 and none in 2027. If the oil rebound lifts inflation further, the median participant may consider a 2027 hike.
Rabobank expects CPI inflation to fall to 2.2% in Q4 2027 based on its energy price forecasts. It pencils in the first cut in March 2028, a second in March 2029 and a third in March 2030.
Rabobank puts the terminal range at 3.25-3.50%, so the FOMC will not cut as far as the 3.2% longer-run median dot implies. It cites the economy's resilience this year.
There is no update to the economic projections in October. The next one is in December.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Rabobank expects a hold with three hawkish dissents. A hold with that many dissents leaves the December hike as the main rate event.
Rabobank's call for the next hike, supported by expected higher CPI inflation from oil.
The Committee hiked and signaled a more hawkish reaction function.

risk_factors: Inflation could climb further because of the recent rebound in oil prices, which could push the median FOMC participant to add a 2027 hike.

A 50 bps move in December is a less likely alternative if the Committee skips October.
